requirements_summary: p99 latency target: <= 100ms for short-turn (<=128 tokens) conversations
throughput: sustained 2k tokens/sec per region during peak, burst cap 50k concurrent requests across regions
cost target: <$0.015 per 1k tokens equivalent at production scale (after batching & quantization savings)
model preferences: open LlamaX-style variants preferred; allow fallback to slightly larger model for degraded contexts
routing needs: region-aware routing + automatic fallback to cheaper model when overloaded
integration: REST/SDK for mobile streaming, function-calling for structured data inserts
observability: token-level cost breakdown, per-route p95/p99, tracing hooks for tracing A->B latency across infra
perf_targets: Benchmark requests: 3 profiles — short (32 tokens), medium (128 tokens), long (512 tokens)
SLOs: p50 < 30ms, p95 < 60ms, p99 < 100ms for short profile on Dedicated config
Quantization goal: evaluate 8-bit and 4-bit quantized variants to measure quality drop <= 2% on intent classification evals
Batching objective: confirm 2-3x token-cost reduction with continuous batching without violating latency SLOs
Caching objective: measure prefix/KV cache hit rate impact on token cost and latency — target 40% cache hit for recurring contexts
poc_plan: Day 0: Share benchmark harness and dataset (synthetic + sampled real sessions).
Day 1: Redwood runs hosted and Dedicated baseline (no quantization, no cache).
Day 2: Redwood enables batching and KV cache; runs quantized model variants on Dedicated.
Day 3: On-prem edge run for APAC residency (small rack) — measure network impact and witness local quantized runtime.
Deliverable: CSV of latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, quality eval scores, and operational notes.
Acceptance: if combined config meets p99 <=100ms and cost target within 10% of estimate -> move to procurement
